# What programs that don't use them link of SQLite, TLS and cryptography, by system, until each is
# cut. `.github/scripts/linkage-check.sh` builds the programs, reads their symbols and fails when a
# program links something not listed here, or no longer links something that is: the pull request
# that cuts one takes its line out.
#
# system program what | why, and the issue that cuts it
macos fs ring-assembly | ring's assembly objects can't be split by function, so -dead_strip keeps about 39 KB of ChaCha20, AES-GCM and bignum code that nothing calls (#1771)
macos hello ring-assembly | the same 39 KB of ring's assembly, in every program (#1771)
linux fs tls | the two functions of rustls's that a hello world links too, the next line's (#1772)
linux hello tls | two of rustls's functions a vtable holds: a TLS payload's drop and `StreamOwned`'s `is_write_vectored` (#1772)
#
# A hello world built for release is held to these sizes, in bytes, as the gate builds it on a Mac
# and CI on Linux and Windows: on Linux and Windows its file's, and on macOS what its sections and
# `__LINKEDIT` hold, without the 16 KB pages' padding (`linkage-check.sh`). Each is what it was measured at, with room to spare: lower it when a
# cut lands, and raise it only knowing what grew.
# system size hello bytes | measured
macos size hello 1340000 | 1,269,146 on 2026-11-26 at 2afb515ab, from the gate's dev build of fennec on arm64: its sections and `__LINKEDIT`, without the pages' padding (the file was 1,285,272)
linux size hello 1050000 | 942,288 on 2026-11-14 in CI on x86-64, and 1,004,464 on aarch64, each from a release build of fennec
windows size hello 1500000 | 1,402,368 on 2026-11-16 in CI at 8e810c58c, from the dev build of fennec; 1,377,792 that morning
